lines.speaker: Inspector Delphine Gault
lines.text: Unsolved Dimensions. The crimes are mild. The dimensions are suspects.

lines.speaker: Inspector Delphine Gault
lines.text: This is Inspector Delphine Gault. I have never closed a case. I have never wanted to.

lines.speaker: Inspector Delphine Gault
lines.text: Unsolved Dimensions, ninety three point nine five. Somebody did something. We may never know who.

lines.speaker: Inspector Delphine Gault
lines.text: Unsolved Dimensions. Lock your doors. And keep your teaspoons where you left them.

lines.speaker: Inspector Delphine Gault
lines.text: Good morning. Roll call. Overnight, eleven new incidents. None solved. A good night's work.

lines.speaker: Constable Pike
lines.text: Inspector, there's been a breakthrough in the case of the warm chair.

lines.speaker: Inspector Delphine Gault
lines.text: Oh dear. How bad?

lines.speaker: Constable Pike
lines.text: Someone's confessed.

lines.speaker: Inspector Delphine Gault
lines.text: Then we'll need to interview them very carefully, Constable, until they're not sure any more.

lines.speaker: Inspector Delphine Gault
lines.text: This is Witness Hour. If you saw something, the lines are open. Please think very carefully before you ring.

lines.speaker: A Witness
lines.text: Inspector? I think I know who moved the moon.

lines.speaker: Inspector Delphine Gault
lines.text: Do you.

lines.speaker: A Witness
lines.text: It was my neighbour. He's got a very long pole, and he's always looking up at it, and...

lines.speaker: Inspector Delphine Gault
lines.text: Madam. Have you considered that you don't?

lines.speaker: A Witness
lines.text: Don't what?

lines.speaker: Inspector Delphine Gault
lines.text: Know. It's very freeing. Try it for a week.

lines.speaker: A Witness
lines.text: ...All right.

lines.speaker: Inspector Delphine Gault
lines.text: Thank you for calling. You've been very unhelpful. It's appreciated.

lines.speaker: Hollis
lines.text: Inspector, it's Hollis Fenn. I'm ringing about my shadow.

lines.speaker: Inspector Delphine Gault
lines.text: Greg.

lines.speaker: Hollis
lines.text: You know him?

lines.speaker: Inspector Delphine Gault
lines.text: Everybody knows Greg, Mister Fenn. He's been seen on the moon. On a beach. At a recital. Every time, he looks a little happier.

lines.speaker: Hollis
lines.text: So you won't find him.

lines.speaker: Inspector Delphine Gault
lines.text: I didn't say that. I said I won't look. He isn't missing. He's travelling. There's a difference, and I've decided to respect it.

lines.speaker: Hollis
lines.text: Could you ask him to send a postcard?

lines.speaker: Inspector Delphine Gault
lines.text: I'll put it in the file.

lines.speaker: Inspector Delphine Gault
lines.text: Cold Cases, Warm Milk. The oldest files in the basement. Pull up a chair. Not that one. It's evidence.

lines.speaker: Inspector Delphine Gault
lines.text: Some of these files are older than the dimensions they happened in. Case file one. A rock was moved. We don't know by whom. We don't know where to.

lines.speaker: Inspector Delphine Gault
lines.text: We have the rock. We have never known where it was. I take it out sometimes, and hold it, and wonder.

lines.speaker: Inspector Delphine Gault
lines.text: To the operator on the relay ship. I'm told you keep a log of everything you hear out there. Good. So do I.

lines.speaker: Inspector Delphine Gault
lines.text: Mine is full of questions. I hope yours is too. Don't answer any of them. Not tonight.

lines.speaker: Inspector Delphine Gault
lines.text: Case file four four one. The Teaspoon. A teaspoon was found in a sugar bowl. Nobody put it there. Nobody who will admit it.

lines.speaker: Inspector Delphine Gault
lines.text: Case file nine. The fridge magnets in a house in the Overlap were rearranged, overnight, to spell hello. The family owns no letter H.

lines.speaker: Inspector Delphine Gault
lines.text: Case file two hundred and six. On the night of the ninth, the moon over Lower Pell was found one inch to the left.

lines.speaker: Inspector Delphine Gault
lines.text: Case file seventy. A ladder was borrowed in good faith. It was returned the following week. One rung taller.

lines.speaker: Inspector Delphine Gault
lines.text: Case file eleven twelve. The Warm Chair. Missus Odile Fenwick came home and sat in her favourite chair, and it was warm. She lives alone. The cat was also surprised.

lines.speaker: Inspector Delphine Gault
lines.text: Case file one hundred. Someone finished a jigsaw in the night. The jigsaw was not ours. Neither, it turns out, was the table.

lines.speaker: Inspector Delphine Gault
lines.text: We found a single footprint at the scene. Size nine. Left foot.

lines.speaker: Inspector Delphine Gault
lines.text: No right foot has ever been recovered. I've stopped looking. Some things walk alone.

lines.speaker: Inspector Delphine Gault
lines.text: We spoke to the neighbours. They said it was a quiet dimension. They always say that.

lines.speaker: Inspector Delphine Gault
lines.text: Every dimension is quiet, until somebody moves something half an inch and doesn't say sorry.

lines.speaker: Inspector Delphine Gault
lines.text: And then, of course, there is the goose. The goose was present. The goose is always present.

lines.speaker: Inspector Delphine Gault
lines.text: I asked the goose where it was on the night in question. The goose has asked for a solicitor.

lines.speaker: Inspector Delphine Gault
lines.text: The dimension itself had no alibi. Asked where it was at the time of the incident, it said: everywhere.

lines.speaker: Inspector Delphine Gault
lines.text: A classic answer. Impossible to disprove. I wrote it down anyway.

lines.speaker: Inspector Delphine Gault
lines.text: Forensics found traces of a substance on the handle. Jam. Strawberry. Possibly raspberry, with ambitions.

lines.speaker: Constable Pike
lines.text: We sent it to the lab, Inspector.

lines.speaker: Inspector Delphine Gault
lines.text: And?

lines.speaker: Constable Pike
lines.text: The lab ate it.

lines.speaker: Inspector Delphine Gault
lines.text: Our only witness was a standard lamp in the hallway. It was switched off at the time. When we switched it on, it had nothing to add.

lines.speaker: Inspector Delphine Gault
lines.text: Its testimony was, however, very illuminating. I won't apologise for that.

lines.speaker: Inspector Delphine Gault
lines.text: A clock in the hall had stopped at twenty past four. Forensics tell me it has always said twenty past four.

lines.speaker: Inspector Delphine Gault
lines.text: That clock has been lying to the family for years. Separate investigation.

lines.speaker: Inspector Delphine Gault
lines.text: I connected the evidence on my board with red string. The clue to the goose. The goose to the moon. The moon, somehow, back to me.

lines.speaker: Inspector Delphine Gault
lines.text: Then I ran out of string. That's usually when you know you're close.

lines.speaker: Constable Pike
lines.text: Inspector, the lab results are back.

lines.speaker: Inspector Delphine Gault
lines.text: And?

lines.speaker: Constable Pike
lines.text: Inconclusive.

lines.speaker: Inspector Delphine Gault
lines.text: Good. Put them with the others, Constable. The tall pile. Mind the goose.

lines.speaker: Inspector Delphine Gault
lines.text: The case remains open. So, I'm told, does the fridge.

lines.speaker: Inspector Delphine Gault
lines.text: The case remains open. If you have any information, please keep it to yourself. We like it like this.

lines.speaker: Inspector Delphine Gault
lines.text: The case remains open. Like all my cases. Like a door in a draughty house that nobody can quite bring themselves to close.

lines.speaker: Inspector Delphine Gault
lines.text: The case remains open. I'll be here. I'm always here.

lines.speaker: Inspector Delphine Gault
lines.text: Goodnight.

lines.speaker: Inspector Delphine Gault
lines.text: I'm often asked why I've never closed a case. It's quite simple. Once a case is closed, it stops being a question and becomes a story.

lines.speaker: Inspector Delphine Gault
lines.text: Stories end. Questions keep you company.

lines.speaker: Inspector Delphine Gault
lines.text: A public appeal. If you see something unusual, say something vague. Something like: that's odd.

lines.speaker: Inspector Delphine Gault
lines.text: Then carry on with your evening. This has been a public appeal.

lines.speaker: Inspector Delphine Gault
lines.text: Unsolved Dimensions is sponsored by Grumbel's Ladders.

lines.speaker: Inspector Delphine Gault
lines.text: Eleven generations of ladders. Not one complaint. Not one incident. Not a single rung out of place.

lines.speaker: Inspector Delphine Gault
lines.text: Which is exactly what worries me. I have a file on them. It's very thin. I check it every night.

lines.speaker: Inspector Delphine Gault
lines.text: Grumbel's Ladders. Up is a choice. So, Mister Grumbel, is down.

lines.speaker: Inspector Delphine Gault
lines.text: Case file thirty one. A pumpkin was found on a doorstep in Gristwick. Its face had been carved from the inside, outwards. No tools were recovered.

lines.speaker: Inspector Delphine Gault
lines.text: The candle inside was lit, and humming. Nobody owns a humming candle.

lines.speaker: Inspector Delphine Gault
lines.text: The pumpkin has been taken into custody. It is being very good about it. It smiles at everyone.

lines.speaker: Inspector Delphine Gault
lines.text: The case remains open. As, I'm afraid, does the pumpkin's mouth.

lines.speaker: Inspector Delphine Gault
lines.text: Halloween week. The busiest week of the year for my department. Doors knock by themselves. Sheets walk about. Children demand sweets with menaces.

lines.speaker: Inspector Delphine Gault
lines.text: Almost none of it is a crime. All of it is unsolved. I love this time of year.

clips.title: The Convergence: A Moon Goes Missing

lines.speaker: Inspector Delphine Gault
lines.text: Case file seven hundred. A moon has gone missing. Every witness agrees one is gone. No two witnesses agree which. Pike?

lines.speaker: Constable Pike
lines.text: Lab results inconclusive, ma'am.

lines.speaker: Inspector Delphine Gault
lines.text: The goose has been brought in. The case remains open.

lines.speaker: Inspector Delphine Gault
lines.text: A smell of toast, reported in every dimension at once.

lines.speaker: Inspector Delphine Gault
lines.text: Nobody has confessed to toasting anything. Somebody is lying. Possibly everybody. The case remains open.

clips.title: The Convergence: The Song Nobody Can Finish

lines.speaker: Inspector Delphine Gault
lines.text: A song, lodged in the head of every witness. Every one of them stops at the same place. Somebody knows how it ends, Pike.

lines.speaker: Constable Pike
lines.text: The goose has been humming it, ma'am.

lines.speaker: Inspector Delphine Gault
lines.text: Of course it has.

lines.speaker: Inspector Delphine Gault
lines.text: Three knocks at the archive door. Constable Pike opened it. Nobody there.

lines.speaker: Inspector Delphine Gault
lines.text: No footprints. No fingerprints. One faint smell of goose. The case remains open.

clips.title: The Convergence: A Colour With No Name

lines.speaker: Inspector Delphine Gault
lines.text: The sky was, briefly, a colour. No witness can name it. Pike has written it down as blue, but suspicious.

lines.speaker: Constable Pike
lines.text: It's the best I could do, ma'am.

lines.speaker: Inspector Delphine Gault
lines.text: A pigeon has entered the archive, walked past the evidence, and sat in my chair. It appears to know me.

lines.speaker: Inspector Delphine Gault
lines.text: I have never seen it before in my life. Which is exactly what it would want me to say.
